orient.title: U.S. citizen — what is different in practice
orient.blurb: U.S. citizens follow the same Croatian foreigners law and stay-and-work permit rules as other third-country nationals. Practical differences are usually: visa-free short entry (cited below), U.S. Embassy Croatia guidance pages, and the U.S. criminal-record process (FBI Identity History Summary). Visa-free presence is not permission to work.

workerDocs.title: U.S.-specific document steps
workerDocs.blurb: Complete these after (or in parallel with) the core worker-document checklist above. Official references: U.S. Embassy Croatia entry & residence page, FBI Identity History Summary Checks, and MVEP granting-stay guidance.

pipeline.label: Set a document pipeline with owners and dates
pipeline.help: Suggested order: (1) order FBI Identity History Summary, (2) apostille, (3) sworn Croatian translation, (4) insurance + photos + accommodation proof, (5) travel/appointments. Put owners on a shared calendar so the labor market test filing window is not wasted.

fbi.label: Order the FBI Identity History Summary (U.S. criminal record)
fbi.help: Croatia typically expects a U.S. criminal-record document for the worker. Use only the official FBI Identity History Summary process. Build in processing time before you need apostille and translation.

apostille.label: Apostille the FBI/civil documents, then get a sworn Croatian translation
apostille.help: After the FBI (and any other U.S. public documents MUP requests) arrive, arrange a Hague apostille, then a court-sworn Croatian translation. Start this early — it often gates the filing date.

embassy.label: Read U.S. Embassy Croatia entry and residence guidance
embassy.help: Use the Embassy page for citizen-facing notes on visa-free stay, residence applications, and registration expectations. It does not replace MUP/HZZ rules for the work permit itself.
embassy.link: U.S. Embassy Croatia — Entry and Residence

visaFree.label: Plan entry under visa-free short-stay rules (still no work)
visaFree.help: U.S. passport holders may enter visa-free for short stays within the cited window. That can help attend appointments in Croatia, but employment still requires the stay-and-work permit. Confirm current wording on MVEP and the Embassy page.

registration.label: Plan accommodation registration after arrival
registration.help: MVEP guidance: accommodation providers generally register guests through eVisitor quickly; if they cannot, the foreigner must self-register within the cited deadline from entry or change of address. Hotels often handle this. This short-stay duty is not the post-permit boravište clock in Step 7. Confirm current MUP/eVisitor practice for your housing type. Cited deadline:

names.label: Keep the legal name identical across every document
names.help: Passport, FBI summary, apostille, translation, employment contract, labor market test request, and stay-and-work forms should show the same legal name spelling. Fix mismatches before filing.

filePermit.title: Filing channel notes (U.S. workers)
filePermit.notes: Many U.S. citizens who are already lawfully present may file in Croatia at the competent police/MUP office after the labor market test. Others may need a consular channel depending on status and MUP instructions. Confirm the correct channel on MUP pages and the U.S. Embassy residence page for this worker. There is no U.S. treaty that lowers Croatian work-permit standards.
